detailed_rationale:
Affle operates a proprietary mobile consumer-intelligence and advertising platform (CPCU - cost-per-converted-user - performance pricing) reaching 3.4+ billion connected devices, evolving under its "Affle 2.0" strategy toward AI-driven consumer intelligence with growing international (developed-market) exposure alongside its India base. The growth trend is genuinely smooth and consistent, not lumpy or acquisition-driven: quarterly sales have risen from Rs.356 Cr (Mar-2023) to Rs.724 Cr (Mar-2026) with profit from Rs.62 Cr to Rs.120 Cr over the same run, and the trailing 1-year growth I calculate from the clean quarterly series (~19.5% revenue, ~19.4% profit) matches our CSV's revenue_growth_1y almost exactly - a good cross-check that this is a real, steady compounding business rather than a base-effect story.

The balance sheet is debt-free (Rs.15 Cr borrowings against Rs.3,624 Cr equity), and the company continues to grow inorganically at the margin - a fresh AdColony asset acquisition was announced in Jul-2026, following the earlier YouAppi integration - consistent with a deliberate ad-tech consolidation strategy rather than a one-off. Two items are worth flagging honestly: working capital days have lengthened from 42.1 to 82.3, a real cash-conversion deterioration (plausibly from a growing international/programmatic mix with longer ad-agency payment cycles, though I could not confirm the specific cause), and promoter holding has drifted down over several years (68.38% in Mar-2020 to 54.91% now) - consistent with ESOP issuance and equity-funded M&A rather than open-market selling, but a real reduction in founder-level ownership concentration nonetheless. The company also pays no dividend, reinvesting fully into growth and M&A.

Reverse-DCF: at ~51x earnings against ROE ~13.8% (5-year average ~16%) and ROCE ~16.8%, the multiple is pricing continued high-teens growth for several more years - a real ask, though supported by a demonstrated multi-year track record of exactly that growth rate, an asset-light model, and an active (if not yet fully proven) international-expansion and M&A strategy.
recommendation_rationale: Quant reads Hold on both lenses (quality_score is notably low at 18.6 despite the debt-free balance sheet and mid-teens ROE, likely reflecting the working-capital deterioration and/or sector-relative ROE comparison). My own work confirms the growth is real and consistent rather than an M&A or base-effect artifact, so there's no case for a Sell; at the same time, growth, while strong, is not accelerating enough nor is quality high enough to create any Hold-vs-Sell tension worth escalating - a straightforward Hold.
summary: Affle is a mobile advertising and consumer-intelligence technology platform with a debt-free balance sheet and a genuinely consistent multi-year growth track record (around 19-20% annually, verified quarter by quarter). The company continues to expand through bolt-on acquisitions (most recently AdColony) and international expansion. The stock is not cheap, and receivables have lengthened somewhat, but the underlying growth story looks real rather than engineered. We rate it a Hold.
positive_para: Affle has delivered remarkably steady, verifiable growth - sales and profit have both roughly doubled over three years without a single lumpy or acquisition-driven jump, a real distinguishing feature versus other 'high growth' names in this batch whose numbers turn out to be base effects. The business is debt-free, asset-light, and continues to add scale through disciplined bolt-on M&A (AdColony, following YouAppi) and international expansion, giving the growth story multiple levers rather than relying on any single market.
negative_para: Working capital days have nearly doubled (42.1 to 82.3), a genuine cash-conversion deterioration that deserves monitoring even though I could not pin down the exact cause, and promoter holding has fallen from 68.38% to 54.91% over six years as the company has funded growth and ESOPs with equity. At ~51x earnings, the stock is priced for continued high-teens growth for several more years, leaving limited room for error, and mobile ad-tech as a category carries structural regulatory/privacy risk (platform-level tracking restrictions) that could pressure the CPCU model over time.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~51x earnings against ROE ~13.8% (5-year average ~16%) and consistent ~19-20% growth, the multiple prices in several more years of high-teens compounding - a real ask but one the company has a genuine multi-year track record of meeting, making this fair-to-somewhat-rich rather than a disconnected re-rating story. Growth is below the 25% hypergrowth threshold, so no dilution/ROE-tier note applies.
